statement.p: Calculate the integral below, if it converges. If it does not converge, enter diverges for your answer.

static.solution: \int_{0}^{\infty} 4x^{2}e^{-x^{3}} dx = \lim_{b \rightarrow \infty} \int_{0}^b 4x^{2}e^{-x^{3}} dx = \left.\lim_{b \rightarrow \infty} \left({{-4} \over 3} e^{-x^3}\right) \right|_0^b = \lim_{b \rightarrow \infty} \left({{-4} \over 3} e^{-b^3} - {{-4} \over 3} e^{-0^3}\right) = 0 + {4\over 3} e^{-0} = {4\over 3} . This integral converges to {4\over 3}.
